title: Tissue extraction from whole caterpillars
author: James JN Kitson
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bz62p9ge

steps.title: Prepare Steel Beads
steps.instruction: Clean and prepare steel ball bearings for tissue grinding.

substeps.instruction: Source hardened carbon steel or stainless steel bearings (one bead per sample tube).
Remove manufacturing oil by baking beads in a borosilicate glass beaker or Duran bottle for at least 12 hours at 250 °C.
Store baked beads in a closed airtight DNA-free container; do not touch with bare hands.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis Buffer 1
steps.instruction: Prepare Lysis Buffer 1 (pH 9) with the following components per 100 mL: 0.701 g Sodium chloride (120 mM), 5 mL 1 M Tris-Hcl (50 mM), 4 mL 0.5 M EDTA (20 mM), and 91 mL H2O.

steps.title: Set Up Collection Tubes
steps.instruction: Prepare collection tubes with beads and Lysis Buffer 1 based on caterpillar size.

substeps.instruction: For medium caterpillars: Use 5 mL screwcap tubes (# 0030122313) with one 4 or 4.5 mm steel bead and 2 mL Lysis Buffer 1.
For smaller caterpillars: Use 2 mL screwcap tubes with two 3 mm beads.
For larger caterpillars: Use 15 mL or 50 mL tubes with larger or multiple steel beads.
Scale Lysis Buffer 1, Lysis Buffer 2, and Proteinase K volumes proportionally to match tube size.

steps.title: Collect Samples
steps.instruction: Place individual caterpillars into the prepared collection tubes using sterile disposable forceps.

substeps.instruction: Label tubes with sample numbers or use barcodes with data collection software (e.g., epicollect5).

steps.title: Sample Transport and Storage
steps.instruction: Store and transport samples to maintain integrity.

substeps.instruction: Place sample tubes in a zip-lock bag and keep cold under dry ice or in a portable freezer.
Caterpillars stored in Lysis Buffer 1 at -20 °C are extractable for at least 6 months.

steps.title: Tissue Homogenization
steps.instruction: Homogenize the larvae using a tissue homogenizer.

substeps.instruction: Defrost tubes containing larvae in Lysis Buffer 1.
Grind larvae (e.g., using Geno/Grinder 2010 at 1750 RPM for 2 minutes) until homogenized.

steps.title: Initial Centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the homogenate at 4,000 x g for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Proteinase Buffer Master Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the Proteinase Buffer master mix consisting of Lysis Buffer 2 and Proteinase K.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Lysis Buffer 2 (pH 9) per 100 mL: 0.701 g Sodium chloride (120 mM), 5 mL 1 M Tris-Hcl (50 mM), 4 mL 0.5 M EDTA (20 mM), 3 g SDS (3%), and 91 mL H2O.
For single samples: Mix 970 μL Lysis solution 2 and 30 μL Proteinase K (10 mg/mL).
For 96-well plates: Mix 102.4 mL Lysis solution 2 and 3.168 mL Proteinase K (10 mg/mL).

steps.title: Digest Tissue
steps.instruction: Add Proteinase Buffer and incubate to digest tissue.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL of freshly-prepared Proteinase Buffer master mix to the lysate and vortex to mix.
Note: If using tubes other than 5 mL, adjust Proteinase Buffer volume to be 1/3 of the Lysis Buffer 1 volume.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight (12-16 hours). For shorter digestion times, increase temperature to 55 °C.
Centrifuge at 4,000 x g for 4 minutes.
Transfer 1.5 mL (single sample) or 1 mL (96-well plate) of supernatant to a clean tube/plate for archiving/backup.
Centrifuge the remaining lysate at 10,000 x g for 1 minute (single sample) or 2,000 x g for 4 minutes (96-well plate).
Transfer 200 μL of the supernatant to a clean 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube or 2.2 mL deep-well 96-well plate. Store remaining lysate at -20 °C.

steps.title: Protein Denaturation
steps.instruction: Denature proteins using a master mix of Protein Denaturation Buffer and ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Protein Denaturation Buffer: 47.7 g Guanidine HCl (5 M) and 100 mL H2O.
Prepare Master Mix: Mix equal parts Protein Denaturation Buffer and 100% Ethanol (220 μL each per sample; for 96-well plate, 42.2 mL or 21.1 mL depending on specific plate volume mentioned).
Add 400 μL of this master mix to each sample or well of a 2.2 mL 96-well plate.
Add the 200 μL of supernatant from the previous step to the denaturation mix.

steps.title: DNA Binding and Washing
steps.instruction: Bind DNA to silica membrane and wash impurities.

substeps.instruction: Load the total sample solution (~600 μL) onto a silica membrane spin column (e.g., NBS Biologicals SD5005 or SD5007).
Centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 minute (or 10 minutes if centrifuge is slower) and discard flow-through.
Add 500 μL Wash Buffer 1, centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1 minute (or 5 minutes if slower), and discard flow-through.
Add 500 μL Wash Buffer 2, centrifuge at 20,000 x g for 3 minutes (or 15 minutes if slower), and discard flow-through.
Prepare Wash Buffer 2 (pH ~7) per 100 mL: 70 mL 100% Ethanol (70%), 1 mL 1 M Tris-Hcl (10 mM), and 29 mL H2O.

steps.title: DNA Elution
steps.instruction: Elute the purified DNA from the membrane.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the spin column to a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube or 0.5 mL DNA collection plate, ensuring the base does not touch the previous collection tube to avoid ethanol contamination.
Add 100-200 μL Elution Buffer directly to the membrane and leave at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Prepare Elution Buffer (pH ~7) per 100 mL: 1 mL 1 M Tris-Hcl (10 mM) and 99 mL H2O.
Centrifuge at ≥ 6000 x g for 1-2 minutes (or 5 minutes if slower).
The DNA is now ready for amplification. Repeat elution steps if higher yield is required.
